description: Using NASA Data to adapt farms for the better!
summary:
AgriPulse is a decision-support concept that turns NASA Earth observation data into practical, location-aware advice for farmers.
The problem: Farmers usually get regional averages, but rainfall, temperature and sunlight can differ greatly over short distances, so a broad forecast may say little about one specific farm.
The data: NASA POWER daily data supplies three groups of variables: solar radiation (drives crop growth and biomass), maximum and minimum temperature (used to calculate heat accumulation), and corrected rainfall and humidity (show rainfall patterns and humidity-related risks).
The model: Two established relationships convert climate data into crop indicators. Growing Degree Days measure accumulated heat, calculated as average daily temperature minus the crop's base temperature, floored at zero. Biomass is proportional to absorbed photosynthetically active radiation times radiation-use efficiency, and a harvest index then relates biomass to economic yield. 
The system: The farmer enters coordinates, crop, farm size and planting date. A Spring Boot backend validates the request, fetches and normalizes NASA POWER data, and returns indicators, a yield range and recommendations through a dashboard.
The roadmap: Phase 1 is an interactive Angular demo with mock data. Phase 2 adds live NASA integration and rule-based advice. Phase 3 refines predictions using regional yield data and local calibration.
